name: Pivot
goal: Turn around out of a dash and stand still
why: A pivot stops a dash on the spot with {char} facing the other way. From the turn {char} can attack, grab, shield or jump as from standing, so {char} can dash away from an opponent and hit back toward them without a dash attack or the landing lag of a wavedash.

tutorial.what: A pivot is a dash turned around with the stick let go on the next frame. {char} does not dash back: the turn plays out and {char} stands, facing the other way.
tutorial.expect: Each pivot is judged when the turn ends: whether the dash was turned, and whether {char} stood or dashed back. After misses, the coach shows the dash and the turn frame by frame.

marks.1: Frame 1: stick to the side. Dash
marks.4: Frame 4: stick back at the center
marks.5: Frame 5: stick smashed the other way. Turn
marks.6: Frame 6: stick let go. No dash back
marks.7: Frame {f}: the turn plays out, {char} standing

lessons.title: Turn, then dash back or stand
text: A dash turned around spends one frame in a turn. On the next frame the game checks the stick: still past 0.8 the other way, {char} dashes back, as in a dash dance. Below 0.8, there is no dash back. The turn plays out with {char} standing, facing the other way: a pivot.

Smash the stick the other way on a frame from the dash's 5th to its {DASH+1}th; a dash from standing ignores the stick for its first 4 frames, and held forward on frame {DASH+1} it becomes a run. Then let the stick go on the next frame. During the turn {char} can attack, grab, shield or jump as from standing.

marks.4: Frame 4: the last frame that ignores the stick
marks.5: Frame 5: stick smashed the other way. Turn
marks.6: Frame 6: stick let go, below 0.8. No dash back
marks.7: Frame {f}: turn. {char} stands, facing the other way

cues.words: Smash the stick the other way
Turn: standing, facing the other way

verdict.success: Pivot: {char} turned and stood, facing the other way.

turned.expect: A turn out of the dash
turned.headline: No turn
turned.fix: Smash the stick the other way during the dash, on a frame from its 5th to its {DASH+1}th. A dash from standing ignores the stick for its first 4 frames, and held forward on frame {DASH+1} it becomes a run, which turns around slowly.

stood.words: the stick was still past 0.8 on the frame after the turn
stood.headline: Dashed back
stood.fix: Let the stick go on the frame after you smash it the other way. Still past 0.8 on that frame, {char} dashes back; below it, the turn plays out and {char} stands.

parts.name: Turn out of the dash
parts.teach: Dash, then smash the stick the other way on a frame from the dash's 5th to its {DASH+1}th. {char} turns for one frame; held, the stick starts a dash back.

marks.5: Frame 5: stick the other way. Turn
marks.6: Frame 6: stick still held. Dash back

coach.note: A dash from standing can be turned from frame 5 to frame {DASH+1}.

parts.name: Let go on the next frame
parts.teach: Smash the stick the other way for one frame only, then let it go. No dash back starts: the turn plays out and {char} stands, facing the other way. Either direction counts.

marks.5: Frame 5: stick the other way. Turn
marks.6: Frame 6: stick let go. No dash back
marks.7: Frame {f}: standing, facing the other way

cues.words: Smash the stick the other way

coach.note: Smash the stick the other way on a frame from 5 to {DASH+1}, and let it go on the next frame: the turn then lasts until {char} stands.
